steps.content: It's already late at night when you leave the detention center. The car belts down the roads of Eastside.
You behave surprisingly like a decent uncle today.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: What, a guy like me can't be a decent uncle?

In the rearview mirror, Levy gives you a dramatic, shocked look. As for Chad, you're certain he didn't get any proper rest worrying constantly in the past few days. Now that he's gotten out on bail, he has soon fallen asleep leaning on Levy.
A nightclub frequenter, sports car hobbyist, and womanizer. Doesn't sound like a decent uncle to me.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I do it for my business. It's called networking, okay?
Levy raises his hand to protest.
I didn't expect you to forgive someone who's harmed you so easily. As far as I know, that's not who you are.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: And who am I?
Someone who's involved in commercial fraud, blackmail, and unfair competition. Your victims are everywhere in Eastside, some of them are even your family.
You're very good at camouflaging yourself with that rich heir disguise. People underestimate you. They don't know what they're getting into when they cross you.
You think you're being so smooth and flawless. But in the face of powerful intelligence, the truth surfaces instantly.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Chief, don't you find it exhausting to live like that?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Of course, we've all been childish and dreamed of being the servant of justice and punishing all crimes and unfairness. It's a satisfying idea. But don't you ever get bored?
This has nothing to do with satisfaction.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hmm, you're right. About the crimes I committed in the past, come and get me once you have the evidence. I promise I won't try to get away with them when the time comes.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: As for today... Today is a good day. Let's put away those depressing thoughts for now, okay?
...Has your empathy been properly fed?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh, more than that. Dear Chief, you can't imagine how wonderful today has been to me. Believe it or not, I haven't had so much fun in years.
Levy's words make you slightly uneasy.
What other fun did you have today?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh, tons. Like seeing you finally developing a sense of humor and Chad realizing his dad is a scumbag. Like knowing what's gonna happen soon...
Levy turns to look at the boy beside him and pushes him gently.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hey, kiddo, wake up. We're home.
The car rounds the corner, and a ruin appears before you. Besides the blazing fire and charred debris, there's nothing there.
Chad blinks his eyes open drowsily. The sight before him shocks him like a blow on the head. It takes him ten seconds to react to what he sees.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: No... No way!
Before the car even stops properly, the boy pushes open the door and stumbles toward the ruin.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahahaha, that silly boy, hahaha... Did you see his face? Oh god, this is killing me, hahaha...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I've held it in for so long just for this moment, hahaha... Oh no, I can't see it clearly from here, I have to get off.
Before you snap out of the shock, Levy swings the door open and catches up with Chad.
When you finally stop the car and find them, Levy is performing the finale of his show.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sigh, my condolences, Chaddy. I also just got the news. A fire broke out at your home earlier today. The cause is not known yet.
Chad is kneeling on the rubble helplessly. He lifts his head, his teary eyes filled only with perplexity and confusion.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But don't worry, no one's hurt. Your dad's not there either. He went missing after getting out of court two days ago. Someone saw him flee on a speedboat last night.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: ...Court?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I forgot to tell you. He was charged with embezzlement a few days ago. The sum was too big, I guess he couldn't handle the stress and fled. Don't worry, nothing can happen to a man like him.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Uncle... Levy... Did you... do it?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hmm? You can say that. It was my money he embezzled, after all. 1.4 billion. I can't just let it slide, can I?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Your dad left in a rush, so he couldn't take too many things with him. If I sell the property under his name, I can cover part of the loss of my company. I'm already thankful for that.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: But... you said...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: What did I say? Oh, I said you're a grown man now. Your dad is a scum, so you must depend on yourself from now on.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Let's call it a day. You're home now. There's nothing more I can help you with.
Levy turns around, but Chad catches his sleeve.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Why...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Huh? Why what? I'm warning you, don't even think about tagging along. Legally, you're not an orphan yet, I'm not gonna adopt you.
Chad doesn't let go.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: But you...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hey, cop, do something with this kid, he won't let me go!
Levy pulls his sleeve free menacingly. Chad loses his balance and falls to the ground.
The next second, Levy assumes his usual frivolous look again.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Let me know if you need anything, Chaddy, though your Uncle Levy may not be of help... Bye.
You stride over to them. Seeing you approach, Levy finally can't hold back his cackles.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahaha, did you see that? Did you see it?
Levy's despicable act infuriates you. You grab his bandaged arm.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Whoa, easy, easy. Why are you suddenly mad?
What did you do?!

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I made an example of him. I'm the owner of an Eastside enterprise, and someone was trying to embezzle my money. If I don't punish him hard, others will want to give it a go too, don't you understand?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But then of course, that's not the point. The point is that it's fun.
Fun? Are you out of your mind?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Looks like you don't get it yet, the most interesting part of this whole thing. I guess humor can't be nurtured in a day. Alright, I'll explain it to you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Look, Chaddy first found out his dad and his good friend weren't exactly good people. He was used, and ended up in prison.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Then, he caught the only lifeline. His uncle, whom he'd hit, forgave him and came to save him, even comforted him. Of course, he was touched and crying happy tears. He now had a family of choice!

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But that didn't last long before he found out his home was on fire, and the uncle he just thought was his savior turned out to be a complete douchebag...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: In just a few days, he lost everything he treasured. And it all happened because he was an idiot. Isn't that super funny? I'm glad I came today so I got to witness this, hahaha...
As he speaks, Levy turns back to look at Chad who's still crying on the ground. He suddenly clicks his tongue and hauls him up.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Stop crying, silly boy. What will crying get you? You should be laughing instead.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: From now on, you're free. Everything that was binding you before is now gone.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Now, go do something. Whatever pleases you, just go and do it.
With that, he lets go of Chad's hand and strides toward the street. Ashen-faced, Chad looks wobbly, as if he may flop down any moment.
Are you alright?
Chad nods and tries his best to keep his balance.

You comfort him with a few simple sentences, but he doesn't look conscious of what you're saying at all. You can only ask the people around to keep an eye on him for now. Meanwhile, Levy has already made it to the corner of the street.
You catch up with Levy. He's leaning against a lamppost, looking relaxed and at ease. The night breeze of Eastside brushes his hair. Seeing your arrival, he waves at you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Ha, you caught me again.
Are you trying to run away?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: It's not like I can get rid of your shackles. I've just seen a good show tonight, so I'm in a great mood. If you let me borrow your car, we can go for a ride. I've missed Eastside's night view. It'll be the icing on the cake.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: What do you say, Chief?
Levy's tone is cheeky. You suppress your irritation and don't respond to his invitation. Instead, you ask a question that's been bothering you.

options: What are you running away from?

choices.text: What are you running away from?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Running away?
Emotions you can't face? Truths you can't say aloud? Or these evil acts even you yourself can't tolerate?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahaha, you just called me a worthless scum minutes ago. Since when do I have moral standards?
You said it yourself. That kid reminds you of your past self.
Ruining your past self with your own hands must feel awful.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Haha... Hahaha...
Suddenly, Levy begins laughing for no reason.
He wipes the corner of his eye with his bandage, keeping an unnaturally wide grin on his face.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahaha... Way to go, Chief. No wonder they all say you're different.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I thought you were gonna blurt out some meaningless bullshit again, things like morals and boundaries... That really hit home, hahaha...
Morals and boundaries are not meaningless...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahaha, coming from you, from your position, that's surprising to hear.
Levy's tone is utterly sarcastic.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Not just morals and boundaries. Trust, kinship, friendship, justice, fairness... All of these are worth nothing in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: The family and friends you trust can backstab you. The justice and fairness you believe in won't even look you in the eye.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sometimes you meet someone you can talk to. But in this hellhole, you always die alone, all by yourself, in the end.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: It's like, you suit up and get ready to go onstage. The collar is stiff and pokes your throat. You've rehearsed for a whole month, and when you see the audience, you get a cramp in your calf. You're afraid you'll mess up and disappoint them.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: And now the organizer tells you the show's canceled because of the rain. You look at the scattering audience and decide to grit your teeth and perform anyway, not missing even a step. But once the show's over, they'll still leave.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: That way of life is too boring. So boring it drives you crazy and makes you wanna set everything on fire.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Everything will disappear in the end. Morals, friendship, everything you spend so much effort in cultivating will eventually end up as useless as toilet paper.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sometimes, I think the world is a game. They made us so short-sighted and ugly, so that when the day comes that they have to destroy us, they can do it guiltlessly.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: If that's the case, why not seize the day and just have fun? Take me as an example, it makes me the happiest to see the thing you treasure get taken away and trampled over. In a hellhole like Eastside, that happens way too often.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: So I live a happy life. I care about nothing but having fun in the moment. What's wrong with that?
Having said that, Levy stands under the street light quietly. Only a light of playfulness and mockery is left in his eyes, as if he's waiting for your response.
Levy assumes a perplexed look, as if really expecting you to tell him what's wrong.
You always say life is meaningless... That may be true.
Yes, we live a meaningless life in the city. My existence may be meaningless too. But meaning is a choice we make.
No matter what you choose, be it wealth, power, fame, dream, justice... or love. It can become the meaning of your existence.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: ...Love? You mean the dopamine that only lasts for three months? The hallucinogen that gives you the illusion that you're not alone? Hahahaha...
That's what you do, pretending you don't care about anything. But you do care about Chad, don't you?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh? What makes you think that?
Everything that Chad cherishes, his father, his friend... and you, his evil uncle. Everyone has only been using him, hurting him.
You've chased all of them away from Chad.
You've said Chad reminds you of your past self. But to you, a soft spot is a weakness, and innocence is a sin... You're playing a life mentor in the way you find apt, aren't you?
You say you don't care about anything, but that's not true. It's just a shame that in the past, you didn't have a caring uncle like yourself.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Haha, are you saying Chad hasn't been through enough? Should I go back to get him and throw him into a private Hypercube mine now?
I won't allow it.
Considering that no one is hurt, I can give you a chance to right the wrongs. Come back with me and make amends for the losses their family has suffered.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: You sound like you're doing baby talk... Is that all?
Levy looks into your eyes in disbelief, and soon gives a laugh of relief.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Alright, I'll go back with you. Even if we can't truly understand each other, we've got no other choice but to stick together. Just like even though my cousin and I are both scumbags, we're still Chaddy's dad and uncle...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I've removed the cancer in my company and had the most fun I've had in years tonight. I suppose this is a good ending.
Don't you feel like you've gained a caring uncle too?
steps.female_content: Don't you feel like you've gained a caring uncle too?

steps.content: Levy can't help but laugh out loud.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Haha, no kidding, it does feel pretty amazing.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: So, when are you gonna bail me out? I'm getting really bored at the Bureau.
Sorry, even as your uncle, I have no say over that. Even if we put aside the other crimes you've committed before...
steps.female_content: Sorry, even as your uncle, I have no say over that. Even if we put aside the other crimes you've committed before...

steps.content: Though no one was hurt, instigation of arson is a crime. I'll investigate whether you were involved in this. If that's the case, then you'll face a criminal charge way worse than Chad's.
Get ready to serve in the Bureau for the rest of your life, my good nephew.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahaha, you've really made progress with your sense of humor.
